Mucubají Lagoon, also known as Mucubaji, lies in the mountainous part of Mérida State. The lake is surrounded by open páramo landscapes: grassy slopes, low-growing vegetation, and the distinctive rosettes of frailejón plants. This cool mountain setting contrasts sharply with Venezuela's tropical savannas and coastline.

The lagoon is a stop on visits to Sierra Nevada National Park. Walks along high-altitude trails begin here, including routes toward Laguna Negra. Views of the lake and surrounding slopes reveal the distinctive scenery of the Venezuelan Andes.

Mutanzi is one of the Indigenous communities encountered on the trek to the Lost City. Meeting local residents offers an opportunity to learn about their daily life and traditions. This is a living community, so the cultural experience is rooted in people's everyday lives as well as the region's ancient archaeological heritage.

The path to Mutanzi passes through mountain and river landscapes. From there, the trail continues toward camps near the Buritaca River. The community is visited as part of a guided trek; the guide explains local traditions and places what travelers see in the wider history of the region's cultures.

Kaieteur National Park is one of Guyana's oldest national parks. It is located not far from the country's capital, Georgetown. Established in 1929 by the British colonial administration, the park was named after Kaieteur Falls, one of the world's most beautiful waterfalls. The waterfall is 270 meters high.

The main purpose of Kaieteur National Park is to preserve its natural landscapes and remarkable flora and fauna. Today, the park covers approximately 60,000 hectares.

## An adventure tour in the national park

### Kaieteur — the jewel of Guyana!

Almost everyone visiting Guyana sees Kaieteur on a day trip from Georgetown. A great option is to combine this excursion with a second stop at nearby Orinduik Falls, where you can relax and swim. The real adventure, however, begins if you decide to stay overnight in this spectacular natural setting.
